title: How a background thread silently ate a login result
author: Kody Wildfeuer (@kody-w)
summary: A historical device-code incident showed why a background poller and an HTTP endpoint must not compete to consume the same authentication result.
audience: Brainstem maintainers and operators diagnosing GitHub device-code sign-in behavior.
prerequisites: Python concurrency basics, a local Brainstem checkout, and familiarity with GitHub device-code authentication.
applicability: Use this pattern when a background worker and an HTTP/UI path need to observe one authentication or job result.
support_boundary: This post explains a design pattern and linked source/tests; it is not an entitlement, account, or production incident support channel.
limitations: This incident note describes one authentication design. It does not guarantee behavior for every OAuth provider, network failure, browser interruption, or future concurrency change.
